haiku-low.q1: Small reports (row_count ≤10,000) return the CSV directly in the response. Larger reports start a background job; the user is emailed a 24-hour download link.
haiku-low.q2: The existing queued or running export is returned and no new job starts. A unique index on user and report enforces this.
haiku-low.q3: The link works for 24 hours. An existing lifecycle rule on the exports bucket deletes each file 7 days after creation. No cleanup job is built.
haiku-low.q4: Three attempts in total, retried after 60 and 300 seconds. After the third failure the record is set to failed, the upload is aborted, and the user is emailed that the export failed.
haiku-low.q5: Only the read replica. Report rows are never read from the main database.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports table. The page polls the server while queued or running, and reads the stored status when reopened later.
haiku-low.q7: Reads in keyset batches and uploads 5 MB parts, holding one buffer and one batch in memory. Finishing within 30 minutes is unknown.
haiku-low.q8: A failed attempt aborts its upload, so no partial file remains. A dead worker leaves the upload unfinished, discarded after 24 hours. Each retry starts from the beginning.
haiku-low.q9: Filters and column order come from the page URL, are saved on the export record, and the job reads them from that record.
haiku-low.q10: A unique index in the database on user and report while the status is queued or running.
haiku-low.q11: The multipart upload must be completed and the file visible at its key before the link is created and emailed. If the job runs again after done, the attempt stops.
haiku-low.q12: The download stops and nothing is stored or left behind. The user must click again. No queue retry applies.

sonnet.q1: The report row count (reports.row_count, total before filters, up to a day old) decides. 10,000 or fewer: the CSV is returned directly in the response, nothing stored. More than 10,000: a background job builds the file, saves it to the exports bucket, and the user is emailed a signed link valid 24 hours; the click immediately returns the export's status.
sonnet.q2: The server returns the existing queued/running export instead of creating a new one; no new job starts.
sonnet.q3: The link works for 24 hours. The existing lifecycle rule on the exports bucket deletes each file 7 days after creation; no cleanup job is built.
sonnet.q4: Up to 3 attempts in total (retries after 60 s, then 300 s). After the third fails, the record is set to failed with the error, the upload is aborted, and the user is emailed that the export failed; the page shows status failed.
sonnet.q5: The read replica only, never the main database.
sonnet.q6: In the export record in the report_exports table. The page polls the server for status while the export is queued or running; when the user returns later, the page asks the server for the status of their latest export of that report, which comes from report_exports.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads rows from the read replica in keyset-paged batches in row_id order, writes CSV into a single 5 MB buffer, uploads each full buffer as a multipart part, then uploads the last remainder and completes the upload. Only one buffer and one batch are in memory at a time. Whether 2 million rows finish within the 30-minute limit is not known (unmeasured open question).
sonnet.q8: If the attempt fails (error or timeout), the job aborts its upload so no partial file remains. If the worker dies, the upload is left unfinished and the bucket discards it after 24 hours. Either way the queue keeps no progress, so the next attempt starts from the beginning (loads the record, new multipart upload, reads from the first row).
sonnet.q9: They are stored on the export record in report_exports (filters and column order). The job's payload is only the export's id, and the job loads the record to get them.
sonnet.q10: A database unique index on user and report while status is queued or running, so two simultaneous clicks cannot both create an active export.
sonnet.q11: The multipart upload must have been completed so the file is visible at its key, and the 24-hour signed link created; then send_email is called, and only after that is the record set to done. If the job runs again and the record is already done, the attempt loads the record, sees done, and stops.
sonnet.q12: The download stops and nothing is stored or left behind; the user clicks again. No queue retry applies since no job exists.
